papers.title: Nature designs tough collagen: Explaining the nanostructure of collagen fibrils
papers.summary: Two competing critical lengths connect molecular adhesion, slip pulses and rupture to fibril strength and dissipation. The main fibril calculations use a two-dimensional, hydrated, cross-link-free reference. Consequently, the explanatory gain is a mechanism map under explicit assumptions, not a comprehensive reconstruction of living tissue. The measured natural molecular length provides external consistency rather than a new experimental test.

representation.rationale: Critical-length ratios organize mechanisms across molecular and fibril scales.
representation.locator: Results: Critical Molecular Length Scales; Figure 5

transfer.rationale: Griffith-style fracture reasoning transfers within mechanics, rather than between distant domains.

formal.rationale: Analytical scaling laws provide no central formal composition constraint.

dynamics.rationale: Loading-induced slip propagation and rupture are central analyzed responses.

organization.rationale: The scientist specifies the multiscale analysis and parameter sweeps.

explanation.rationale: Competing slip and rupture scales discriminate failure mechanisms.

validation.rationale: Atomistically parameterized mesoscopic simulations test predictions; no new fabrication.

robustness.rationale: Lengths, adhesion, cross-links and geometries vary; physiological alternatives remain open.
robustness.locator: Results: Bimolecular Assemblies; Larger Collagen Fibrils

surprise.observation: Stronger adhesion can eventually favor brittle molecular rupture.
surprise.interpretation: Maximizing bond strength alone need not maximize toughness.
surprise.boundary: Model mechanics do not establish evolutionary optimization.

detail.observation: The slip threshold shifts from roughly 42 nm in pairs to 200 nm in fibrils.
detail.consequence: Boundary conditions and confinement change the inferred design scale.

papers.title: Nanoconfinement controls stiffness, strength and mechanical toughness of β-sheet crystals in silk
papers.version: Nature Materials 9, 359–367; published online March 14, 2010; author-hosted advance publication PDF
papers.summary: Nanoconfinement makes weak hydrogen bonds cooperate through uniform shear and repeated bond reformation. The comparison tests pure bending against combined shear and bending, making the added mechanism consequential. Critical strand length also bounds how far crystal dimensions can grow. Cited experimental shear moduli were not measured on individual silk nanocrystals, limiting the directness of validation.

representation.rationale: Crystal size and strain distribution explain collective bond performance.

transfer.rationale: Continuum shear–bending theory interprets molecular deformation within mechanics.

formal.rationale: No categorical composition or transport constraint drives the contribution.

dynamics.rationale: Bending, pull-out and stick–slip trajectories are central analyzed responses.

organization.rationale: Fixed computational experiments do not reorganize a discovery workflow.

explanation.rationale: Strain localization and cooperative rupture distinguish small from large crystals.

validation.rationale: Molecular dynamics and DFT support mechanics; experiments are external comparisons.

robustness.rationale: Alternative beam models, size sweeps and pulling rates discriminate mechanisms.
robustness.locator: Figure 3; Methods: Application of boundary conditions

surprise.observation: Smaller crystals can simultaneously improve stiffness, strength and dissipation.
surprise.interpretation: Weak-bond architecture can overcome constituent weakness.
surprise.boundary: Nanocrystal behavior is not a complete model of whole silk.

detail.observation: Experimental-rate pull-out forces require an estimated sixfold reduction; the transition length survives rate variation.
detail.consequence: The robust claim concerns the mechanism and length scale, rather than raw simulated force.

read: Main PDF results, figures, Table 1 and methods

references.scope: Main paper, figures, methods and rate limitations

papers.title: Category Theoretic Analysis of Hierarchical Protein Materials and Social Networks
papers.summary: A shared categorical description makes selected protein-failure and communication-failure mechanisms explicitly comparable. This is a qualitative transfer of deliberately simplified structure–function relations. The authors acknowledge that added detail could break the correspondence. The useful advance is stating which relations must survive a translation; identical abstract organization does not establish identical chemistry or empirical behavior.

representation.rationale: Typed relations replace a solely constituent-based account of functionality.

transfer.rationale: Protein hidden length maps explicitly to backup social communication.

formal.rationale: Commuting diagrams and fiber products constrain meanings and composition.

dynamics.rationale: Failure under extension or noise is analyzed qualitatively.

organization.rationale: Researchers construct representations; no adaptive discovery process is executed.

explanation.rationale: A latent lifeline explains retained function after weak links fail.

validation.rationale: The social case is constructed; prior protein mechanics motivate examples.

robustness.rationale: With/without-lifeline comparisons are illustrative, not broad empirical tests.

surprise.observation: A slack connection can be functionally invisible until another connection fails.
surprise.interpretation: The useful abstraction includes conditional function, beyond connectivity.
surprise.boundary: The social example was deliberately designed to match the protein olog.

detail.observation: Figure 4 alone omits essential equalities and fiber-product definitions in Tables 1–2.
detail.consequence: A similar-looking graph is insufficient to establish the claimed correspondence.

read: Main methods and results; supporting-figure descriptions
notRead: Separate supplemental PDFs; cited original mechanics studies

papers.title: Categorical prototyping: incorporating molecular mechanisms into 3D printing
papers.summary: The abstract reports transferring selected molecular mechanics into printed, experimentally tested macroscopic models; full methods were unavailable. These provisional entries distinguish an explicit experimental claim from an audited experimental result. Unknown formal or robustness support remains unranked. The abstract describes preserving a subset of mechanics, which is a narrower objective than reproducing the entire molecular material or establishing a universal translation guarantee.

representation.rationale: A prototype preserves selected model properties across physical realizations.

transfer.rationale: The reported correspondence connects nanoscale models and macroscopic printed structures.

formal.rationale: Formal preservation conditions cannot be rated from the abstract.

dynamics.rationale: Detailed temporal or modal targets were not reviewed.

organization.rationale: Workflow organization was not described in reviewed material.

explanation.rationale: Mechanistic discrimination needs the unretrieved results and controls.

validation.rationale: The abstract explicitly reports printing and mechanical experimental validation.

robustness.rationale: Replication, uncertainty and alternatives could not be checked.

surprise.observation: The abstract reports examining a twisted physical prototype beyond the original model.
surprise.interpretation: A faithful partial embodiment may suggest additional questions.
surprise.boundary: This observation has not been checked against full results.

detail.observation: Only chosen mechanical properties are claimed to be retained.
detail.consequence: Geometric resemblance would not warrant assuming all nanoscale properties transfer.

notRead: Publisher full text blocked; methods, figures and supplements unavailable
